title: perch: every eidolon started with --config also gets EIDOLON_CONFIG naming the same file
why: The subagent plugin (eidolon-plugins SA1) reads EIDOLON_CONFIG to give a child the parent's config; without it a child spawned from a Minerva door runs under ~/.config/eidolon/config.toml and escapes Minerva's policy, guard rows and sessions dir. eidolon reads no EIDOLON_CONFIG itself, so the variable is inert for everything but plugins that ask for it.
what:
Every place the perch builds a Command for eidolon:
- spawn.rs (the door, about line 241; argv() pushes --config when config is Some), pending.rs (about line 615), runs/proc.rs (about line 155), titles.rs (about line 69), guard/mod.rs (about line 222), mode.rs (about lines 270 and 332). Find any other with `grep -rn 'Command::new' perch/src`.
- When the argv carries `--config <file>`: `.env("EIDOLON_CONFIG", <file>)`, the exact same path (absolute, as passed).
- When it carries no --config: `.env_remove("EIDOLON_CONFIG")`, so a value inherited from the operator's shell can never point a child at another config.
- Nothing else in the env changes (NO_PROXY handling in spawn.rs stays).
- The path is never a secret; no token goes in the env (unchanged rule).
- Doc comments beside each site and the README rows that describe a child's environment (perch/src/README.md, perch/src/runs/README.md if it lists the env) say it in one line.
owns_files: perch/tests/*.rs (new tests only; never tests/common/mod.rs or tests/http.rs)
tests: A unit test per site (or per builder function) that builds the Command the way the code does and asserts via as_std().get_envs() (tokio) or get_envs() (std): EIDOLON_CONFIG is Some(the --config path) when a config is given, and is explicitly removed (get_envs yields ("EIDOLON_CONFIG", None)) when not. If a site's Command is built inline in a function that also spawns, factor out only the builder, the smallest change. One integration test, if fake_eidolon can report its env without new fake features, that a door started by the perch sees EIDOLON_CONFIG equal to its --config; otherwise say why not and do not change the fakes.
live_check: None needed beyond the suite (no route changes).
risk: Low. A wrong path would point subagent children at the wrong config; the tests pin it to the --config argument.
